source_text: Domus in vico sine muro sicut ager — semper redimi potest. Humilitas aperta redemptori. Christus ager noster.
thought_title: The unwalled house as humility open to redemption
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical redemption rules to the soul, contrasting the walled city house with the unwalled village house.
pass_a_gloss: A house in a village without a wall is like a field — it can always be redeemed. Humility is open to the redeemer. Christ is our field.

choices.why: The source contrasts a walled city with an unwalled settlement; 'village' preserves the rural, unprotected sense.
The comparison to a field is the point: the unwalled house has the same perpetual redeemability as agricultural land.
The passive infinitive with 'potest' expresses ongoing possibility; 'always' renders 'semper' explicitly.

choices.english: Humility is open to the redeemer
choices.why: The nominative 'Humilitas' with the adjective 'aperta' and dative 'redemptori' is a compact statement; the rendering keeps the noun as subject and the dative as the one to whom it is open.
rejected: Humility lies open to the redeemer

choices.why: The three-word sentence is a theological identification; 'our field' keeps the possessive and the agricultural metaphor.
rejected: Christ is the field for us

bible_refs.note: Houses in villages without walls are to be treated as fields and may be redeemed at any time.

pass_b_english: A house in an unwalled village can always be redeemed, just like a field (Leviticus 25:31). Humility stands open to the redeemer. Christ is our field.

last_rejected.quote: Humility stands open to the redeemer
last_rejected.why: Latin 'aperta' modifies 'humilitas' as predicate nominative, not a verb; 'stands open' adds unsupported verbal construction.
last_rejected.fix: Open humility [is] for the redeemer, or: Humility, laid bare, [belongs] to the redeemer.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Aperta' is predicate adjective with 'humilitas'; 'stands open' is normal English rendering of the adjective, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: English drops explanatory connection: source presents Christ as 'ager noster' in apposition/explanation, but 'our field' loses the anaphoric link to 'field' in the lemma.
last_rejected.fix: Christ is our field [that is, the field].
last_rejected.ruling: 'Christus ager noster' = 'Christ is our field'; no anaphoric word exists in source. English faithfully renders the Latin.
